mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, just think for a moment about the journey we've shared—tracing that winding road through Sierra Leone and Liberia. It's more than just a path on a map. It's a living, breathing reminder of how strong the human spirit can be, even in the face of challenges most of us can barely imagine. The stories we've heard aren't just about survival. They're about that quiet, steady hope that keeps people moving, day after day. So as you reflect, ask yourself—what does it really mean to listen deeply, to bear witness, and to carry forward the wisdom of those who've walked much tougher roads? Here are a few things that really stand out: Real resilience? It's found in those small, everyday acts of courage and kindness. Our histories, no matter how heavy, don't have to shape our futures. Justice and healing—they aren't places you arrive at, but journeys you keep walking. And true belonging? It's built one connection at a time—to people, to place, and to memory. Most of all, hope isn't about grand gestures. It's about showing up, again and again, in ordinary life. So as you head back into your world, remember—the spirit we've encountered together isn't tied to one country, one story, or one community. It's alive wherever someone faces hardship with dignity, reaches out with kindness, or builds something lasting—even when the future feels uncertain. These lessons aren't just for travelers or outsiders. They're for anyone who's ready to see the world with open eyes and an open heart. Let these stories inspire you. When your own path looks tough, remember: that resilient spirit we found in West Africa? It's in all of us. You just have to take the next step.
